The NFL and CTE latest
stories.summary:
I’m hesitant to post this but it’s relevant. CTE article and study results I found Al-Shaair’s comments particularly interesting.
	 



	I told this story on here before but I have a good friend who was a LB. He was a fringe roster guy / teams guy. He kicked around for 7 seasons. He was like a Buffalo Joe type. He told me a story about his concussions. If I’m remembering correctly he had 7 that he knew about. The hardest hit of his career was not one of them. He was covering a kick and got absolutely lit up. He didn’t see the guy. He started walking to the wrong sideline. One of his teammates grabbed him and directed him to the right place. He had no idea where he was for like 5-10 minutes. He tried to stay away from everyone on the sideline because he didn’t want them to know. Eventually his mind cleared and he finished the game. What he said, and has stuck with me was, “I was a fringe roster guy making about $1M a year. This was towards the end of my career. If I come out, I may never get back out there. I’m the ideal cut candidate at that point. I can be replaced by a rookie and they’d save money. I needed to do everything in my power to never show injury to protect my earnings.” That happens all the time in the NFL.
	 



	Was that the right or wrong decision? There’s no easy answer. In one sense, he was risking his health and future every play. In the other breath, he made enough money in those 7 years, plus his pension, that he never has to work again if he doesn’t want to. He isn’t rich by any means but can give his family a decent life on that. Was it worth it? He’s gone back and forth on that but is adamant that he would do the same thing over.



	 



	This is a topic that we all have strong feelings about. Please remain respectful to other posters as you share your thoughts.

Joey Porter Jr. - should he be a trade target?
stories.summary:
Excellent press man CB with crazy length, at a contract impasse in Pittsburgh with a new staff. Flip them Hairston? IGB and a pick? What would it take?



	 



	My thought is that CBs that can operate on an island are key for Leonhard's defense, especially to give time for the exotic pressures do their thing. Hairston has tools and is promising but is more of a zone corner, definitely not a press man CB. We didn't get a blue chipper on the DLine, but putting an elite physical CB opposite Benford could do wonders for the pass rush on third and long.



	 



	Of all the elite defenders that have come available via trade this offseason, this one could actually work with a 2026 cap charge that wouldn't require anyone to restructure and his age shouldn't spook Beane on what would surely be a large extension required. Lot of $ to tie up at boundary CB I understand with Benford already paid, but it's a piece that would actually move the needle IMO and Beane could then feel free to keep throwing high picks at DLine hoping one will actually hit one of these days 🤣

stories.title: (PSA) Micah Hyde now on Buffalo Plus podcast weekly...
stories.summary:
I think many of you enjoy this podcast with Mike Catalana, Jenna Cottrell, and Dan Fetes. Well, they scored a coup (IMO) by landing Micah for the season in a weekly (Wednesday) segment. On today's episode he shared his thoughts on preseason and some other stuff, and he confirmed what a lot of us thought -- some teams actually do scheme for preseason and when they do it completely throws off what you're trying to accomplish. He specifically cited the game at Pittsburgh 2 or 3 years ago...said the Steelers obviously gameplanned and the Bills hadn't even said the word "Pittsburgh" at all during camp. He said they went out there and were like "WTF?" and it completely skewed what they wanted to accomplish.



	 



	Micah's a Bill through and through...last week he shared a lot of insight as to what went down in his last season (PS) and the conversations he had with Beane and McDermott about whether he would play or not. Unfortunately they didn't ask him what he thought of McD getting canned but today he definitely implied something needed to change to get the Bills "over the hump."



	 



	The other thing I like about this podcast is that this trio are not beholden to the Bills so they'll say what they don't like (they all seem to dislike the Nickel City unis), but they totally downplayed the stadium hoopla and said they are going to check things out for themselves on Saturday.
